properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured on main): add_change_event publishes a decoy `description` parameter so the handler can redirect the commonest mistake. find_tools lists it among the tool's parameter names, which is all a door agent sees, so the catalogue invites the mistake. 0.78.0's argument check passes it as valid, so a call with other shape errors is told "every one is listed" and is refused for `description` on the next call
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-10-05, triaging art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05 (tool surface). Binaries: 0.76.0 and 0.78.0 release builds, and main at e7e304d (reports 0.78.0); scratch stores under the hub session's scratchpad, isolated HOME.

① OBSERVED, the reporter's words (2026-10-01, 0.76.0): "ChangeEvent discovery included `description`, but submission refused: a ChangeEvent has no `description`. The prose goes in `summary`." Expected: discovery names only real fields.

② PRECEDENT: fact:defect-the-commonest-changeevent-mistake-was-fixed-in-the-description-and-a-third-project-hit-it-anyway (2026-09-05). Its fix, chg:three-additive-surface-fixes-from-field-feedback (#429), made `description` an accepted parameter only so the handler could refuse it naming `summary` and `rationale`. Nothing records the decoy's effect on find_tools.

③ CANDIDATES: (a) find_tools lists every schema property, decoy included; (b) the agent read stale docs; (c) the 0.78.0 schema check treats the decoy as valid; (d) the observation is wrong.

⑤ MEASURED.
- `find_tools {query: "record a change event"}` on 0.76.0 and main lists add_change_event's parameters as [affected, change_type, commits, description, detected_at, id, name, rationale, rationale_basis, repair, stands_in_for, subject, summary]. (a) holds; find_tools builds `parameters` from the input schema's property keys (crates/reflow2-mcp/src/tools/query.rs ~983).
- On main, a call with description plus a bare-string `affected`, subject "code" and rationale_basis "measured" is refused listing 3 problems, "every one is listed, so the call can be fixed in one round trip". `description` is not among them. The corrected call is then refused for `description`. (c) holds: two round trips where the reply promised one.
- The decoy is the only one: a sweep of main's 195 input schemas for "NOT A REAL FIELD" found add_change_event.description alone.

⑥ CLASS: a containment placed in the published schema to teach at refusal time is, to every reader of the schema's names (find_tools, the argument check, a client building a form), indistinguishable from a real field. The redirect works; where it lives makes it a lure. A fix at the class keeps the redirect and takes the decoy out of what the schema advertises (or marks it so find_tools and the argument check treat it as an error with its redirect).

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether an MCP client that renders schemas also offers `description` to its model. Only find_tools and the door were measured.
